text:
ali: heads-up — saw a weird eviction cascade in ap-southeast1 at ~02:10 UTC. cluster-autoscaler dropped ~30 gpu nodes in ~3m after a flurry of pod term signals, tons of coldstarts for inference routes.

maria: ugh. saw spikes in tail latency too (>=2.5s p99). is this the same network flap from the provider?

jay: quick summary from node events: a short control-plane outage led to kubelet heartbeats jittering, CA interpreted as long drain and started scale-down. preemptible node pools + aggressive downscale = bad combo.

sam: can we roll a temporary hotfix to avoid 0->scale transitions? suggest increasing "scaleDownUnneededTime" and adding a staged eviction window for gpu nodepools.

lee: proposal: tiered cooldowns by nodepool label `gpu-tier`: critical (no scale-to-zero), shared (staggered snooze), burst (aggressive). also add a KV-cache-preserve signal to reject evictions if pods report active kvcache=true.

ali: ooh I like kvcache signal. current problem is eviction assumes idle because pod cpu is low but kvcache warming is stateful and costly to rebuild.

maria: implementation questions — how do we surface kvcache state to CA? annotate pods? a sidecar health endpoint?

jay: two minimal options: 1) controller sets a node annotation when any pod reports `/internal/keepalive` true; CA webhook reads annotation and delays scale-down. 2) use pod annotation + CA filter by `--ok-to-evict` logic. 1 feels less invasive.

sam: +1 for node annotation; less churn. rough sketch: controller watches pods with label `app=inference`, queries `/metrics` for `kvcache_entries > 0` and flips node annotation `redwood/gpu-keepalive=true`.

lee: also add time-decay: keepalive TTL of 5m after last active metric so we don't hold forever. and a cool-down stagger per AZ to avoid total regional loss.

ali: what about autoscaler params? current `scaleDownUnneededTime: 5m`, `scaleDownUtilizationThreshold: 0.5`. Suggest bump to `10m` for gpu-tier=shared and set `maxEmptyBulkDelete` to 2 to avoid deleting many nodes at once.

maria: can we do a configmap-per-pool so we can tune remotely? or use nodepool annotations that our autoscaler infra reads?

jay: configmap-per-pool + operator to sync -> easiest for rolling changes. I'll draft a kustomize snippet.

sam: add a safety fallback: if API server flaps, don't act on scale decisions for 2m. basically a CA circuit-breaker that requires stable control-plane to run large deletes.

lee: we should also emit a metric `gpu_eviction_cascade_count` and alert at >1 in 6h. want a postmortem iff cascade triggered user-visible errors.

ali: agree. immediate action items:
- jay: prototype node-annotation controller + TTL (PR by EOD)
- sam: patch CA config for staged cooldowns + maxEmptyBulkDelete (canary to eu-west)
- maria: add Grafana panel for kvcache-active nodes + gpu_eviction_cascade_count
- lee: write quick runbook steps for oncall (how to pause CA + apply annotation override)

sre-bot: incident created: #INC-2026-314 — tracing ap-southeast1 eviction cascade. pagerduty notified.

maria: cool. one more ask — can we tag nodepools with `cost-profile=reserved|spot|burst` and make scale policies conservative on reserved? helps cost/control tradeoffs.

sam: good call. reserved pools should never scale to zero unless explicitly allowed. I'll include that in the operator design.

ali: thanks team. if anyone observes another spike, ping here and include `kubectl get nodes -o wide` + `kubectl describe pod` for one of the affected inference deploys.

jay: putting up a quick PR link in a bit: https://git.redwood.company/r/eng/keepalive-controller/pull/42 :draft

lee: :thumbsup: will start a runbook doc after we validate the canary.
